assumptions: Quality scores are Phred at the stated offset.
The adapter given is the one ligated.
limits: Trims; it does not filter contaminants or correct bases.
bio.jane/contract.question: What do these FASTQ reads look like after the adapters and low-quality ends are trimmed, and how much was removed?

description: Trim sequencing adapters and low-quality ends off FASTQ reads before mapping, and report what was removed. This is cutadapt's algorithm: quality trimming is BWA's running-sum rule (not a threshold - a single bad base in a good tail is absorbed, a real decline is not), and the adapter is found by semiglobal alignment allowing errors, so a PARTIAL adapter at the very end of a read is caught where a substring search would miss it. Quality trimming runs FIRST and adapter removal second, which is cutadapt's own order and changes the result when a low-quality tail is also the start of an adapter. THE REPORT ATTRIBUTES EVERY REMOVED BASE TO THE STEP THAT REMOVED IT, because losing 30% of your bases to quality means a bad sequencing run and losing it to adapter means a short insert - different problems that one total cannot distinguish. It does not map anything and does not filter reads: a read trimmed to nothing is returned empty and counted, never silently dropped.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

adapter.description: the adapter sequence to remove. Unset means quality trimming only. Illumina TruSeq is AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCAC and Nextera is CTGTCTCTTATACACATCT.

adapter_kind.description: which end the adapter sits at. A read running off the end of its insert hits the 3' adapter, which is why that is the default.

max_error_rate.description: errors allowed in the adapter match, as a fraction of the overlap. cutadapt's own default. Advanced.

min_length.description: reads shorter than this after trimming are COUNTED as too short, not removed - this tool does not filter. 0 reports none. Advanced.

min_overlap.description: an adapter overlap shorter than this is ignored. Low values trim real bases by chance - at 1, a read ending in the adapter's first base is 'trimmed'. Advanced.

phred_offset.description: quality encoding: 33 for every modern FASTQ, 64 only for pre-1.8 Illumina. Advanced.

quality_cutoff_back.description: quality cutoff for the 3' end, where quality decays with cycle number. 0 is off; 20 is the usual choice. NOT a threshold on individual bases - see the description.

quality_cutoff_front.description: quality cutoff for the 5' end, which fails for different reasons than the 3' end and so takes its own number. 0 is off, and off is the usual answer. Advanced.

reads.description: the reads to trim, as FASTQ - quality lines are required, because both halves of this need them.

name: trim_reads

basesRemovedByAdapter.description: bases removed by adapter trimming alone

basesRemovedByQuality.description: bases removed by quality trimming alone

readsEmptied.description: reads trimmed to nothing at all - a different alarm from 'too short', because it usually means the read was all adapter

readsWithAdapter.description: how many reads carried the adapter - the number that says whether your insert size is shorter than your read length

report.description: what was removed and by which step: bases before and after, the two attributed counts, reads with an adapter, reads emptied and reads left too short

trimmedFastq.description: the trimmed reads as FASTQ, ready for `map_reads`
